How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

217	CREATE SEQUENCE claim_listed_seq START WITH 1;
218	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN listed BIGINT DEFAULT NEXT VALUE FOR claim_listed_seq NOT NULL;
219	== V28__grade_terms.sql
220	-- A grade's own terms on a sheet: the days after a claim's date that a claim of a person of that grade
221	-- is due by. A grade with no row here uses the sheet's terms.
222	CREATE TABLE grade_terms (
223	    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
224	    grade    VARCHAR(1)   NOT NULL,
225	    terms    INT          NOT NULL,
226	    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, grade)
227	);

229	-- date plus its sheet's terms.
230	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN due_by DATE;
231	UPDATE claim c SET due_by = DATEADD(DAY, (SELECT s.terms FROM sheet s WHERE s.id = c.sheet_id), c.claim_date);
232	ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN due_by SET NOT NULL;
233	== V29__claim_log.sql
234	-- A claim's status log: one row per status it has had (its DRAFT row written when it is added), who moved
235	-- it there, the sheet's today then, and its due as computed at that moment (null when it had none).
236	CREATE TABLE claim_log (
237	    id       BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
238	    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
239	    claim_id BIGINT       NOT NULL,
240	    status   VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
241	    by_user  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
242	    on_date  DATE         NOT NULL,
243	    due      DECIMAL(19, 2)
244	);
245	CREATE INDEX claim_log_sheet ON claim_log (sheet_id, claim_id, id);
246	== V30__person_hold.sql
247	-- A person's holds: each runs from its from-date to its to-date (both inclusive; no to-date: open-ended).
248	-- A person may have several over time. While a hold covers a claim's date, that claim, if open (OPEN or
249	-- PENDING) and not bound by a statement, counts in no live total. A person held before holds were dated
250	-- keeps a hold from the beginning of time (a null from-date).
251	CREATE TABLE person_hold (
252	    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
253	    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
254	    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
255	    from_date DATE,
256	    to_date   DATE
257	);
258	CREATE INDEX person_hold_person ON person_hold (person_id, id);

260	ALTER TABLE person DROP COLUMN held;
261	== V31__rate_to.sql
262	-- A rate can carry a to-date: it applies through that date (null: with no end). A claim dated after
263	-- the to-date of the rate that would apply to it (the latest from-date on or before the claim's date)
264	-- has no rate; an earlier rate does not come back.
265	ALTER TABLE rate ADD COLUMN to_date DATE;
266	== V32__claim_stated_na.sql
267	-- A claim a statement bound to n/a: it had no due then because the rate that would apply to it had
268	-- ended (its date after that rate's to-date). It shows and totals as n/a (a total skips it) until the
269	-- next statement rebinds or unbinds it, even once a later rate is in force on its date. (A claim
270	-- bound with no figure for want of any rate keeps a live due, as before.)
271	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN stated_na BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
272	== V33__cap.sql
273	-- A sheet's cap: a person's due-total is at most it (two decimals; null means no cap).
274	ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN cap DECIMAL(12, 2);
275	== V34__period_person_total.sql
276	-- Each person's due-total for a closed period, fixed when it was closed, for every person on the sheet
277	-- then (0.00 for one with nothing in it). Dropped when the period is reopened.
278	CREATE TABLE period_person_total (
279	    period_id BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES period (id),
280	    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
281	    person_id BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
282	    total     DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL,
283	    PRIMARY KEY (period_id, person_id)
284	);
285	== V35__dated_settings.sql
286	-- A sheet's dated settings: each value a setting that carries a figure (clerk-limit, floor, terms,
287	-- terms-<grade>, late-pct, cap) has from a from-date. The value in force on a date is the one with the
288	-- latest from-date on or before it; before every from-date the setting has its starting value (floor
289	-- 1.00, late-pct 0.00, terms 14; none for the others). A null value is a blank one (no limit, no cap, a
290	-- grade using the sheet's terms).
291	CREATE TABLE setting_value (
292	    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
293	    setting_key VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
294	    from_date   DATE         NOT NULL,
295	    setting     VARCHAR(20),
296	    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date)
297	);
298	
299	-- The settings already set hold from the beginning of time.
300	INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
301	    SELECT id, 'clerk-limit', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(clerk_limit AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE clerk_limit IS NOT NULL;
302	INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
303	    SELECT id, 'floor', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(floor AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE floor <> 1.00;
304	INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
305	    SELECT id, 'terms', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(terms AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE terms <> 14;
306	INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
307	    SELECT id, 'late-pct', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(late_pct AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE late_pct <> 0.00;

309	    SELECT id, 'cap', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(cap AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE cap IS NOT NULL;
310	INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
311	    SELECT sheet_id, 'terms-' || grade, DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(terms AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM grade_terms;
312	
313	ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN clerk_limit;
314	ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN floor;
315	ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN terms;
316	ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN late_pct;
317	ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN cap;
318	DROP TABLE grade_terms;
319	== V36__claim_deferred.sql
320	-- The date an OPEN claim is deferred until (null when it was never deferred). Until the sheet's today
321	-- reaches it the claim counts in no total, is not overdue, cannot be settled and a statement leaves it
322	-- unbound; from that day on it is an OPEN claim like any other.

324	== V37__claim_proofs.sql
325	-- How many proofs a claim has been given (raised by one at a time; 0 for a claim given none). A claim whose
326	-- due is above the sheet's proof threshold (a dated setting, key proof-threshold) in force on its date cannot
327	-- be settled or approved while it has none.
328	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN proofs INT DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;
329	== V38__permission.sql
330	-- A sheet's permission matrix: for an action (open, settle, void, reassign, close, reopen), the roles
331	-- that may take it, a comma separated list (e.g. clerk,steward). An action with no row keeps the
332	-- standing rule: open, settle, void and close by clerk and steward; reassign and reopen by steward.
333	CREATE TABLE sheet_permission (
334	    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
335	    action    VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
336	    roles     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
337	    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, action)
338	);
339	== V39__grace_days.sql
340	-- A sheet's grace days (null means off; not dated): when the sheet's today is changed, every open period
341	-- whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today is closed.
342	ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN grace_days INT;
343	== V40__claim_split_from.sql
344	-- For a claim split off another, the number of the claim it was split from (null otherwise).
345	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN split_from VARCHAR(200);
346	== V41__person_watch.sql
347	-- The people a user watches, per sheet. A watcher is told (a NOTIFY audit line) when one of the person's
348	-- claims is settled, approved or re-settled; watchers are told in the order they started watching (by id).
349	CREATE TABLE person_watch (
350	    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
351	    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
352	    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
353	    user_name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
354	    UNIQUE (person_id, user_name)
355	);

358	-- A steward's delegation of the steward role to a user, from its from-date to its to-date (both inclusive).
359	-- While the sheet's today is inside the range the user acts as a steward in every rule, and each audit line
360	-- of a change they make (not one that only reports figures) ends with for=<the steward who delegated>.
361	CREATE TABLE delegation (
362	    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
363	    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
364	    user_name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
365	    by_user   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
366	    from_date DATE         NOT NULL,
367	    to_date   DATE         NOT NULL
368	);
369	CREATE INDEX delegation_user ON delegation (sheet_id, user_name);
370	== V43__sheet_archived.sql
371	-- An archived sheet: a steward has archived it. Everything on it stays visible and every change to it is
372	-- refused (only watching, which is the user's own, is left).
373	ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN archived BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
374	== V44__person_terms.sql
375	-- A person's own terms: the days after a claim's date that it is due by, ahead of their grade's and
376	-- the sheet's terms. Null when they have none.
377	ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN terms INT;
378	== V45__claim_lock.sql
379	-- Who holds a claim's editor open: the signed-in user whose edit button locked it for everyone else,
380	-- until they save or cancel it or the sheet's today changes. Null when the claim is not locked.
381	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN locked_by VARCHAR(255);
382	== V46__period_soft_closed.sql
383	-- Whether a period is soft-closed: its due-total (closed_total) and each person's figure for it
384	-- (period_person_total) are fixed, but claims dated inside it can still be changed. A claim added
385	-- while the period its date falls in is soft-closed is a late entry.
386	ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN soft_closed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
387	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN late_entry BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
388	== V47__statement_history.sql
389	-- Each statement taken of a person, numbered 1, 2, ... in the order taken, with its due-total (as shown,
390	-- so possibly 'n/a') and date. The person's stated_total and statement_date are those of the highest
391	-- numbered one; cancelling the last statement removes it, and the person then shows the one before it
392	-- (or nothing). A statement taken before this table only has its last one recorded.

394	    sheet_id       VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
395	    person_id      BIGINT NOT NULL,
396	    seq            BIGINT NOT NULL,
397	    due_total      VARCHAR(20),
398	    statement_date DATE NOT NULL,
399	    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, person_id, seq)
400	);

403	    WHERE statement_count > 0 AND statement_date IS NOT NULL;
404	== V48__history.sql
405	-- The sheet's history, for a statement taken as of a past date: each change is kept with the sheet's
406	-- today when it was made (on_date), in the order made (id). The state as of the end of a date is what
407	-- the changes made while the sheet's today was on or before it left. What was there before this
408	-- history was kept counts from the beginning of time (0001-01-01).
409	
410	-- A person counts from the sheet's today when they were added.
411	ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN added_on DATE DEFAULT DATE '0001-01-01' NOT NULL;
412	
413	-- A hold counts from the sheet's today when it was given.
414	ALTER TABLE person_hold ADD COLUMN held_on DATE DEFAULT DATE '0001-01-01' NOT NULL;
415	
416	-- A claim's values after each change to it (the ones its figures and statement binding depend on).
417	CREATE TABLE claim_history (
418	    id             BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
419	    sheet_id       VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
420	    on_date        DATE           NOT NULL,
421	    claim_id       BIGINT         NOT NULL,
422	    person_id      BIGINT         NOT NULL,
423	    amount         DECIMAL(14, 2) NOT NULL,
424	    claim_date     DATE           NOT NULL,
425	    status         VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
426	    settled_due    DECIMAL(19, 2),
427	    stated         BOOLEAN        NOT NULL,
428	    stated_due     DECIMAL(19, 2),
429	    stated_na      BOOLEAN        NOT NULL,
430	    corrects       VARCHAR(600),

432	    deferred_until DATE
433	);

435	INSERT INTO claim_history (sheet_id, on_date, claim_id, person_id, amount, claim_date, status, settled_due, stated,
436	        stated_due, stated_na, corrects, due_by, deferred_until)
437	    SELECT sheet_id, DATE '0001-01-01', id, person_id, amount, claim_date, status, settled_due, stated, stated_due,
438	        stated_na, corrects, due_by, deferred_until FROM claim ORDER BY id;
439	
440	-- Each rate set: it replaces the grade's rate from the same from-date.
441	CREATE TABLE rate_history (
442	    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
443	    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
444	    on_date   DATE          NOT NULL,
445	    grade     VARCHAR(1)    NOT NULL,
446	    pct       DECIMAL(7, 2) NOT NULL,
447	    from_date DATE,
448	    to_date   DATE
449	);
450	CREATE INDEX rate_history_sheet ON rate_history (sheet_id, id);
451	INSERT INTO rate_history (sheet_id, on_date, grade, pct, from_date, to_date)

453	
454	-- Each grade given to a person: it replaces the one they had from the same from-date.
455	CREATE TABLE grade_history (
456	    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
457	    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
458	    on_date   DATE         NOT NULL,
459	    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL,
460	    grade     VARCHAR(1)   NOT NULL,
461	    from_date DATE
462	);
463	CREATE INDEX grade_history_sheet ON grade_history (sheet_id, person_id, id);
464	INSERT INTO grade_history (sheet_id, on_date, person_id, grade, from_date)
465	    SELECT sheet_id, DATE '0001-01-01', person_id, grade, from_date FROM person_grade;
466	
467	-- Each dated setting value recorded: it replaces the one recorded from the same from-date.
468	CREATE TABLE setting_history (
469	    id          BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
470	    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
471	    on_date     DATE         NOT NULL,
472	    setting_key VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
473	    from_date   DATE         NOT NULL,
474	    setting     VARCHAR(20)
475	);
476	CREATE INDEX setting_history_sheet ON setting_history (sheet_id, id);
477	INSERT INTO setting_history (sheet_id, on_date, setting_key, from_date, setting)
478	    SELECT sheet_id, DATE '0001-01-01', setting_key, from_date, setting FROM setting_value;
479	
480	-- Each policy date set (null: blank, the sheet's today).
481	CREATE TABLE policy_history (
482	    id          BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
483	    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
484	    on_date     DATE         NOT NULL,
485	    policy_date DATE
486	);
487	INSERT INTO policy_history (sheet_id, on_date, policy_date)
488	    SELECT id, DATE '0001-01-01', policy_date FROM sheet WHERE policy_date IS NOT NULL;
489	
490	-- Each retirement of a person.
491	CREATE TABLE retire_history (
492	    id           BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
493	    sheet_id     VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),

495	    person_id    BIGINT       NOT NULL,
496	    retired_from DATE         NOT NULL
497	);

499	    SELECT sheet_id, DATE '0001-01-01', id, retired_from FROM person WHERE retired_from IS NOT NULL;
500	== V49__row_change.sql
501	-- Every change to a row of a sheet, for showing the sheet as of a past date (see history/AsOfView): each
502	-- insert, update or delete of a row of a sheet's tables, kept in the order made (id) with the sheet's
503	-- today when it was made (on_date) and the row's values before and after (each a serialized Object[] in
504	-- the table's column order; old_row null for an insert, new_row null for a delete). The rows are
505	-- captured by a trigger on each table (history/RowCapture), installed at start-up.
506	CREATE TABLE row_change (
507	    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
508	    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
509	    on_date    DATE         NOT NULL,

511	    old_row    VARBINARY(1000000),
512	    new_row    VARBINARY(1000000)
513	);

515	
516	-- The tables a sheet's view is replayed into: one per captured table, created at start-up.
517	CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS asof;
518	== V50__entry_date.sql
519	-- A sheet's entry date (null means off): while it is set, it is the default date of a new claim (the
520	-- claim form, the quick-add bar, a pasted line with a blank date and a correction) instead of the
521	-- sheet's today. Not dated.
522	ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN entry_date DATE;
523	== V51__claim_reminded.sql
524	-- The last day (the sheet's today then) a reminder was written for a claim; null when never reminded. An OPEN or
525	-- PENDING claim can be reminded once per sheet-today.
526	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN reminded DATE;
527	== V52__holiday.sql
528	-- The sheet's holidays: a claim's due-by, fixed when it is created, that falls on one is moved to the next
529	-- day that is not a holiday. Each date is on the sheet's list at most once.
530	CREATE TABLE holiday (
531	    sheet_id     VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
532	    holiday_date DATE         NOT NULL,

534	);
535	== V54__claim_ref.sql
536	-- A claim's external reference (null: none). A reference is used at most once on a sheet, comparing
537	-- without regard to case (checked by the app).
538	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN ref VARCHAR(600);
539	== V55__claim_tags.sql
540	-- A claim's tags: trimmed, lower-cased, without repeats, sorted and comma separated (null: none).
541	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN tags VARCHAR(2000);
542	
543	-- Every tag ever used on a sheet (a tag stays here when the claims carrying it change).
544	CREATE TABLE sheet_tag (
545	    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
546	    tag      VARCHAR(600) NOT NULL,
547	    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, tag)
548	);
549	== V56__void_reason.sql
550	-- The reason a VOID claim was voided with, chosen from its sheet's void reasons (null: none given).
551	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN void_reason VARCHAR(600);
552	
553	-- The sheet's void reasons, trimmed, in the order they were added: while there is one, voiding a claim needs
554	-- one of them. Each reason is on the sheet's list at most once.
555	CREATE TABLE void_reason (
556	    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
557	    position INT          NOT NULL,
558	    reason   VARCHAR(600) NOT NULL,
559	    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, reason)
560	);
561	== V57__claim_comment.sql
562	-- A claim's comments, oldest first: the text (trimmed, never empty), who wrote it and the sheet's today then.
563	CREATE TABLE claim_comment (
564	    id       BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
565	    sheet_id VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
566	    claim_id BIGINT        NOT NULL,
567	    by_user  VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL,
568	    on_date  DATE          NOT NULL,
569	    text     VARCHAR(2000) NOT NULL
570	);
571	CREATE INDEX claim_comment_sheet ON claim_comment (sheet_id, claim_id, id);
572	== V58__claim_edited_by.sql
573	-- Who last edited a claim: the signed-in user whose save (the claim form or the row's amount entry) last changed it. Null until edited.
574	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN edited_by VARCHAR(255);
575	== V59__settle_batch.sql
576	-- Settle batches: a bulk settle that settles (or sends to PENDING) at least one claim is the sheet's next
577	-- batch, numbered 1, 2, ... in the order they happen. The sheet keeps the number of its last batch (null
578	-- when there has been none), and each claim settled by a batch keeps its number (null when settled one at a time).
579	ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN last_batch INT;
580	ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN batch INT;
581	== V60__person_contact.sql
582	-- A person's contact: stored trimmed and lower-cased, unique on its sheet. Null when they have none.
583	ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN contact VARCHAR(500);
584	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX person_sheet_contact ON person (sheet_id, contact);
585	== V61__person_alias.sql
586	-- A person's aliases: other names they are known by on the sheet. An alias shares the names' uniqueness
587	-- (ignoring case, no alias equals any name or alias on the sheet), checked when one is added.
588	CREATE TABLE person_alias (
589	    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
590	    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
591	    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
592	    alias     VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL
593	);
594	CREATE INDEX person_alias_sheet ON person_alias (sheet_id, person_id);
595	== V62__claim_template.sql
596	-- A sheet's claim templates: a name (unique on the sheet; saving it again replaces the template), an
597	-- amount (0.00 or more, two decimals) and a note. A claim made from one copies its amount and note then.
598	CREATE TABLE claim_template (
599	    sheet_id VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
600	    name     VARCHAR(500)   NOT NULL,
601	    amount   DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount >= 0),
602	    note     VARCHAR(2000)  NOT NULL,
603	    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, name)
604	);
605	== V63__pool.sql
606	-- A sheet's pools: a name (unique on the sheet, trimmed, not blank).
607	CREATE TABLE pool (
608	    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
609	    name     VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
610	    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, name)
611	);

613	-- at most 100.00, two decimals), listed in the order they were added (by id). A retired member's share
614	-- counts as 0.00 toward the pool's total.
615	CREATE TABLE pool_member (
616	    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
617	    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
618	    pool_name VARCHAR(500)  NOT NULL,
619	    person_id BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
620	    share     DECIMAL(5, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (share > 0 AND share <= 100),
621	    UNIQUE (sheet_id, pool_name, person_id)
622	);
623	== V64__pot.sql
624	-- A sheet's pot (two decimals; null means none; not dated): each member of a balanced pool gets a cut of it.
625	ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN pot DECIMAL(12, 2);
626	== V65__patron_order.sql
627	-- The order a person named their patrons in (the first-named takes a share's remainder).
628	CREATE SEQUENCE patron_seq;
629	ALTER TABLE patron ADD COLUMN seq BIGINT DEFAULT NEXT VALUE FOR patron_seq NOT NULL;

631	-- A sheet's parent sheet (null means none; not dated): a grade with no rate in force on a date on the sheet
632	-- takes its parent's rate for that grade and date, then the parent's parent's, up to three levels up.
633	ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN parent_id VARCHAR(200);

spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.password=
# Pooled connections are never retired: when HikariCP closes one at its default 30 min
# max-lifetime, this in-memory H2 closes under the remaining sessions and every later statement
# fails with "The database has been closed" while the health probe stays UP. 0 means no lifetime.
spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=0

# Flyway owns the schema. JPA does not create tables.
spring.flyway.enabled=true
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=none
# Close the persistence context at the end of the request, not during view rendering.
spring.jpa.open-in-view=false

# Readiness probe.
management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health
management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true

# The SPA is served from src/main/resources/static (built there by bin/build); deep-link
# fallback is in SpaConfig.java.

# Audit sink: one record per line to this known file, so tests assert side-effects by reading it.
# bin/start passes an absolute path via AUDIT_FILE; default is .run/audit.log.
app.audit.file=${AUDIT_FILE:.run/audit.log}
== V1__sheet.sql
-- A sheet: everything else in the app is kept per sheet, keyed by its id. A row is made the
-- first time an id is loaded; a sheet never loaded before starts empty.
CREATE TABLE sheet (
    id         VARCHAR(200) PRIMARY KEY,
    created_by VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL
);
== V2__sheet_today.sql
-- The sheet's own "today": every date decision and default date in the sheet uses it, never the
-- real clock. A sheet starts on the real date it was made.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN today DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE NOT NULL;
== V3__person.sql
-- People on a sheet, listed in the order they were added (by id). A grade is one of A, B or C.
CREATE TABLE person (
    id       BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    name     VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
    grade    VARCHAR(1)   NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX person_sheet ON person (sheet_id, id);
== V4__person_name_unique.sql
-- A person's name is unique on its sheet, compared without regard to case (names are stored trimmed).
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN name_key VARCHAR(500) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (LOWER(name));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX person_sheet_name ON person (sheet_id, name_key);
== V5__claim.sql
-- A person's claims: an amount (0.00 or more, two decimals), a date and a note (may be empty).
-- Listed newest first (by id, descending).
CREATE TABLE claim (
    id         BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id   VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id  BIGINT         NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    amount     DECIMAL(14, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount >= 0),
    claim_date DATE           NOT NULL,
    note       VARCHAR(2000)  DEFAULT '' NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX claim_sheet ON claim (sheet_id, id);
== V6__rate.sql
-- A sheet's rate for each grade: a percent with two decimals (0.00 or more). A grade has at most
-- one rate; setting it again replaces it. A grade with no row has no rate.
CREATE TABLE rate (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    grade    VARCHAR(1)    NOT NULL,
    pct      DECIMAL(7, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (pct >= 0),
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, grade)
);
== V7__claim_status.sql
-- A claim's status: DRAFT (new) -> OPEN -> SETTLED; a DRAFT or OPEN claim can be VOID.
-- Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward the totals.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(10) DEFAULT 'DRAFT' NOT NULL;
== V8__claim_number.sql
-- A claim's number: given when it is opened, the next on its sheet (1, 2, ...), never reused.
-- A draft has none; voiding a claim clears it. sheet.claim_number is the last number given.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN claim_number BIGINT DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN claim_no BIGINT;
== V9__claim_settled_due.sql
-- A settled claim's due, fixed when it is settled: its amount at its person's grade's rate then.
-- Null while the claim is not settled, or when the grade had no rate (its due then stays live).
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN settled_due DECIMAL(19, 2);
== V10__rate_from.sql
-- A rate can carry a from-date: a grade may have several rates, each in force from its from-date
-- (a rate with none applies from the beginning of time). A grade has at most one rate per from-date
-- (setting it again replaces it); the store keeps that, as a null from-date cannot be in a key.
ALTER TABLE rate ADD COLUMN from_date DATE;
ALTER TABLE rate DROP PRIMARY KEY;
CREATE INDEX rate_sheet_grade ON rate (sheet_id, grade, from_date);
== V11__claim_opened_by.sql
-- Who opened a claim: the signed-in user who moved it from DRAFT to OPEN. Null until it is opened.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN opened_by VARCHAR(255);
== V12__person_version.sql
-- The version of a person's stored values: starts at 1 and goes up by one each time they are
-- saved, so an editor that loaded an older version is refused rather than overwriting a newer save.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN version BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;
== V13__statement.sql
-- A person's statements: how many have been taken, and the last one's due-total (as shown, so
-- possibly 'n/a') and date (the sheet's today when it was taken). Null until the first statement.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN statement_count BIGINT DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN stated_total VARCHAR(20);
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN statement_date DATE;
-- A claim bound by its person's last statement: it shows and totals stated_due (the figure it had
-- then; null when it had none, its due then staying live) until the next statement rebinds or
-- unbinds it.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN stated BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN stated_due DECIMAL(19, 2);
== V14__period.sql
-- A sheet's periods: a name, unique on the sheet without regard to case (stored trimmed), and a
-- from- and to-date, both inclusive (from on or before to). No two periods of a sheet overlap; the
-- app keeps that, as the store cannot.
CREATE TABLE period (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    name      VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
    name_key  VARCHAR(500) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (LOWER(name)),
    from_date DATE         NOT NULL,
    to_date   DATE         NOT NULL,
    CHECK (from_date <= to_date)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX period_sheet_name ON period (sheet_id, name_key);
== V15__period_closed.sql
-- Whether a period is closed, and the due-total fixed when it was closed (null while open). No claim
-- dated inside a closed period can be added, edited, opened, settled or voided.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN closed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN closed_total DECIMAL(19, 2);
== V16__person_retired.sql
-- The date a person is retired from (null while not retired). A person with a date set counts as
-- retired at once, whatever the date; no claim of theirs may be dated after it.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN retired_from DATE;
== V17__person_held.sql
-- Whether a person is on hold: while held, their OPEN claims count in no live total (their SETTLED
-- claims still do).
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN held BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;
== V18__settings.sql
-- A sheet's clerk limit: a clerk can settle a claim only when its due is at or below it (two
-- decimals; null means no limit).
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN clerk_limit DECIMAL(12, 2);

-- The role a user name holds on a sheet: clerk or steward. A name with no row is a clerk.
CREATE TABLE sheet_role (
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    user_name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    role      VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, user_name)
);
== V19__floor.sql
-- A sheet's floor: a claim's live due is at least it (two decimals). It starts at 1.00.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN floor DECIMAL(12, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.00;
== V20__terms.sql
-- A sheet's terms: the number of days after a claim's date that it is due by. It starts at 14.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN terms INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 14;
== V21__late_pct.sql
-- A sheet's late percent: an overdue claim's due gains it (of its figure) for every full 30 days
-- it is overdue (two decimals). It starts at 0.00.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN late_pct DECIMAL(9, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00;
== V22__patron.sql
-- A person's patrons: other people on the same sheet they have named, each at most once.
CREATE TABLE patron (
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    patron_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    PRIMARY KEY (person_id, patron_id)
);
CREATE INDEX patron_sheet ON patron (sheet_id);
== V23__person_grade.sql
-- A person's grade is dated: each grade they are given is in force from its from-date (the first
-- one, with none, from the beginning of time) until the next one's. A person has at most one grade
-- per from-date (giving one again replaces it). person.grade keeps the grade they were first given;
-- the grade in force on a date is read from here.
CREATE TABLE person_grade (
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    grade     VARCHAR(1)   NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE
);
CREATE INDEX person_grade_person ON person_grade (person_id, from_date);
INSERT INTO person_grade (sheet_id, person_id, grade, from_date) SELECT sheet_id, id, grade, NULL FROM person;
== V24__claim_correction.sql
-- A claim with a negative amount is a correction: it names, by number, the SETTLED claim of the
-- same person it corrects. The amount loses its 0.00-or-more check (rebuilt without it), and a
-- claim keeps the number it corrects (null for an ordinary claim).
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN amount_signed DECIMAL(14, 2);
UPDATE claim SET amount_signed = amount;
ALTER TABLE claim DROP COLUMN amount;
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN amount_signed RENAME TO amount;
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN amount SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN corrects BIGINT;
== V25__policy_date.sql
-- A sheet's policy date: a claim dated before it rounds half up, one on or after it half to even.
-- Null (blank) means the sheet's today.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN policy_date DATE;
== V26__period_numbering.sql
-- A sheet's period numbering from-date (null means off): while it is set and the sheet's today is on
-- or after it, a claim opened is numbered within the period its date falls in, <period name>-<n>, or
-- X-<n> when in no period. Claim numbers (and the number a correction corrects) become text.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN period_numbering_from DATE;
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN claim_no SET DATA TYPE VARCHAR(600);
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN corrects SET DATA TYPE VARCHAR(600);

-- The last number given in each of a sheet's period sequences, keyed by period id ('X' for claims in
-- no period). Never reused.
CREATE TABLE claim_sequence (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    seq_key  VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL,
    last_no  BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, seq_key)
);
== V27__claim_listed.sql
-- Where a claim is listed: claims are listed newest first by this key, which a new claim takes on insert
-- and a reassigned claim takes afresh, so it lists as its new person's newest claim whatever its date.
CREATE SEQUENCE claim_listed_seq START WITH 1;
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN listed BIGINT DEFAULT NEXT VALUE FOR claim_listed_seq NOT NULL;
== V28__grade_terms.sql
-- A grade's own terms on a sheet: the days after a claim's date that a claim of a person of that grade
-- is due by. A grade with no row here uses the sheet's terms.
CREATE TABLE grade_terms (
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    grade    VARCHAR(1)   NOT NULL,
    terms    INT          NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, grade)
);
-- A claim's due-by, fixed when it is created from the terms then in force; an existing claim takes its
-- date plus its sheet's terms.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN due_by DATE;
UPDATE claim c SET due_by = DATEADD(DAY, (SELECT s.terms FROM sheet s WHERE s.id = c.sheet_id), c.claim_date);
ALTER TABLE claim ALTER COLUMN due_by SET NOT NULL;
== V29__claim_log.sql
-- A claim's status log: one row per status it has had (its DRAFT row written when it is added), who moved
-- it there, the sheet's today then, and its due as computed at that moment (null when it had none).
CREATE TABLE claim_log (
    id       BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    claim_id BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    status   VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    by_user  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    on_date  DATE         NOT NULL,
    due      DECIMAL(19, 2)
);
CREATE INDEX claim_log_sheet ON claim_log (sheet_id, claim_id, id);
== V30__person_hold.sql
-- A person's holds: each runs from its from-date to its to-date (both inclusive; no to-date: open-ended).
-- A person may have several over time. While a hold covers a claim's date, that claim, if open (OPEN or
-- PENDING) and not bound by a statement, counts in no live total. A person held before holds were dated
-- keeps a hold from the beginning of time (a null from-date).
CREATE TABLE person_hold (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    from_date DATE,
    to_date   DATE
);
CREATE INDEX person_hold_person ON person_hold (person_id, id);
INSERT INTO person_hold (sheet_id, person_id, from_date, to_date) SELECT sheet_id, id, NULL, NULL FROM person WHERE held;
ALTER TABLE person DROP COLUMN held;
== V31__rate_to.sql
-- A rate can carry a to-date: it applies through that date (null: with no end). A claim dated after
-- the to-date of the rate that would apply to it (the latest from-date on or before the claim's date)
-- has no rate; an earlier rate does not come back.
ALTER TABLE rate ADD COLUMN to_date DATE;
== V32__claim_stated_na.sql
-- A claim a statement bound to n/a: it had no due then because the rate that would apply to it had
-- ended (its date after that rate's to-date). It shows and totals as n/a (a total skips it) until the
-- next statement rebinds or unbinds it, even once a later rate is in force on its date. (A claim
-- bound with no figure for want of any rate keeps a live due, as before.)
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN stated_na BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
== V33__cap.sql
-- A sheet's cap: a person's due-total is at most it (two decimals; null means no cap).
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN cap DECIMAL(12, 2);
== V34__period_person_total.sql
-- Each person's due-total for a closed period, fixed when it was closed, for every person on the sheet
-- then (0.00 for one with nothing in it). Dropped when the period is reopened.
CREATE TABLE period_person_total (
    period_id BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES period (id),
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    total     DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (period_id, person_id)
);
== V35__dated_settings.sql
-- A sheet's dated settings: each value a setting that carries a figure (clerk-limit, floor, terms,
-- terms-<grade>, late-pct, cap) has from a from-date. The value in force on a date is the one with the
-- latest from-date on or before it; before every from-date the setting has its starting value (floor
-- 1.00, late-pct 0.00, terms 14; none for the others). A null value is a blank one (no limit, no cap, a
-- grade using the sheet's terms).
CREATE TABLE setting_value (
    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    setting_key VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    from_date   DATE         NOT NULL,
    setting     VARCHAR(20),
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date)
);

-- The settings already set hold from the beginning of time.
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
    SELECT id, 'clerk-limit', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(clerk_limit AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE clerk_limit IS NOT NULL;
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
    SELECT id, 'floor', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(floor AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE floor <> 1.00;
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
    SELECT id, 'terms', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(terms AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE terms <> 14;
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
    SELECT id, 'late-pct', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(late_pct AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE late_pct <> 0.00;
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
    SELECT id, 'cap', DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(cap AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM sheet WHERE cap IS NOT NULL;
INSERT INTO setting_value (sheet_id, setting_key, from_date, setting)
    SELECT sheet_id, 'terms-' || grade, DATE '0001-01-01', CAST(terms AS VARCHAR(20)) FROM grade_terms;

ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN clerk_limit;
ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN floor;
ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN terms;
ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN late_pct;
ALTER TABLE sheet DROP COLUMN cap;
DROP TABLE grade_terms;
== V36__claim_deferred.sql
-- The date an OPEN claim is deferred until (null when it was never deferred). Until the sheet's today
-- reaches it the claim counts in no total, is not overdue, cannot be settled and a statement leaves it
-- unbound; from that day on it is an OPEN claim like any other.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN deferred_until DATE;
== V37__claim_proofs.sql
-- How many proofs a claim has been given (raised by one at a time; 0 for a claim given none). A claim whose
-- due is above the sheet's proof threshold (a dated setting, key proof-threshold) in force on its date cannot
-- be settled or approved while it has none.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN proofs INT DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL;
== V38__permission.sql
-- A sheet's permission matrix: for an action (open, settle, void, reassign, close, reopen), the roles
-- that may take it, a comma separated list (e.g. clerk,steward). An action with no row keeps the
-- standing rule: open, settle, void and close by clerk and steward; reassign and reopen by steward.
CREATE TABLE sheet_permission (
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    action    VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    roles     VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, action)
);
== V39__grace_days.sql
-- A sheet's grace days (null means off; not dated): when the sheet's today is changed, every open period
-- whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today is closed.
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN grace_days INT;
== V40__claim_split_from.sql
-- For a claim split off another, the number of the claim it was split from (null otherwise).
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN split_from VARCHAR(200);
== V41__person_watch.sql
-- The people a user watches, per sheet. A watcher is told (a NOTIFY audit line) when one of the person's
-- claims is settled, approved or re-settled; watchers are told in the order they started watching (by id).
CREATE TABLE person_watch (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    user_name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (person_id, user_name)
);
CREATE INDEX person_watch_sheet ON person_watch (sheet_id, user_name);
== V42__delegation.sql
-- A steward's delegation of the steward role to a user, from its from-date to its to-date (both inclusive).
-- While the sheet's today is inside the range the user acts as a steward in every rule, and each audit line
-- of a change they make (not one that only reports figures) ends with for=<the steward who delegated>.
CREATE TABLE delegation (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    user_name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    by_user   VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE         NOT NULL,
    to_date   DATE         NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX delegation_user ON delegation (sheet_id, user_name);
== V43__sheet_archived.sql
-- An archived sheet: a steward has archived it. Everything on it stays visible and every change to it is
-- refused (only watching, which is the user's own, is left).
ALTER TABLE sheet ADD COLUMN archived BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
== V44__person_terms.sql
-- A person's own terms: the days after a claim's date that it is due by, ahead of their grade's and
-- the sheet's terms. Null when they have none.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN terms INT;
== V45__claim_lock.sql
-- Who holds a claim's editor open: the signed-in user whose edit button locked it for everyone else,
-- until they save or cancel it or the sheet's today changes. Null when the claim is not locked.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN locked_by VARCHAR(255);
== V46__period_soft_closed.sql
-- Whether a period is soft-closed: its due-total (closed_total) and each person's figure for it
-- (period_person_total) are fixed, but claims dated inside it can still be changed. A claim added
-- while the period its date falls in is soft-closed is a late entry.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN soft_closed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN late_entry BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
== V47__statement_history.sql
-- Each statement taken of a person, numbered 1, 2, ... in the order taken, with its due-total (as shown,
-- so possibly 'n/a') and date. The person's stated_total and statement_date are those of the highest
-- numbered one; cancelling the last statement removes it, and the person then shows the one before it
-- (or nothing). A statement taken before this table only has its last one recorded.
CREATE TABLE person_statement (
    sheet_id       VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id      BIGINT NOT NULL,
    seq            BIGINT NOT NULL,
    due_total      VARCHAR(20),
    statement_date DATE NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (sheet_id, person_id, seq)
);
INSERT INTO person_statement (sheet_id, person_id, seq, due_total, statement_date)
    SELECT sheet_id, id, statement_count, stated_total, statement_date FROM person
    WHERE statement_count > 0 AND statement_date IS NOT NULL;
== V48__history.sql
-- The sheet's history, for a statement taken as of a past date: each change is kept with the sheet's
-- today when it was made (on_date), in the order made (id). The state as of the end of a date is what
-- the changes made while the sheet's today was on or before it left. What was there before this
-- history was kept counts from the beginning of time (0001-01-01).

-- A person counts from the sheet's today when they were added.
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN added_on DATE DEFAULT DATE '0001-01-01' NOT NULL;

-- A hold counts from the sheet's today when it was given.
ALTER TABLE person_hold ADD COLUMN held_on DATE DEFAULT DATE '0001-01-01' NOT NULL;

-- A claim's values after each change to it (the ones its figures and statement binding depend on).
CREATE TABLE claim_history (
    id             BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id       VARCHAR(200)   NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    on_date        DATE           NOT NULL,
    claim_id       BIGINT         NOT NULL,
    person_id      BIGINT         NOT NULL,
    amount         DECIMAL(14, 2) NOT NULL,
    claim_date     DATE           NOT NULL,
    status         VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
    settled_due    DECIMAL(19, 2),
    stated         BOOLEAN        NOT NULL,
    stated_due     DECIMAL(19, 2),
    stated_na      BOOLEAN        NOT NULL,
    corrects       VARCHAR(600),
    due_by         DATE           NOT NULL,
    deferred_until DATE
);
CREATE INDEX claim_history_sheet ON claim_history (sheet_id, claim_id, id);
INSERT INTO claim_history (sheet_id, on_date, claim_id, person_id, amount, claim_date, status, settled_due, stated,
        stated_due, stated_na, corrects, due_by, deferred_until)
    SELECT sheet_id, DATE '0001-01-01', id, person_id, amount, claim_date, status, settled_due, stated, stated_due,
        stated_na, corrects, due_by, deferred_until FROM claim ORDER BY id;

-- Each rate set: it replaces the grade's rate from the same from-date.
CREATE TABLE rate_history (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    on_date   DATE          NOT NULL,
    grade     VARCHAR(1)    NOT NULL,
    pct       DECIMAL(7, 2) NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE,
    to_date   DATE
);
CREATE INDEX rate_history_sheet ON rate_history (sheet_id, id);
INSERT INTO rate_history (sheet_id, on_date, grade, pct, from_date, to_date)
    SELECT sheet_id, DATE '0001-01-01', grade, pct, from_date, to_date FROM rate;

-- Each grade given to a person: it replaces the one they had from the same from-date.
CREATE TABLE grade_history (
    id        BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id  VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    on_date   DATE         NOT NULL,
    person_id BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    grade     VARCHAR(1)   NOT NULL,
    from_date DATE
);
CREATE INDEX grade_history_sheet ON grade_history (sheet_id, person_id, id);
INSERT INTO grade_history (sheet_id, on_date, person_id, grade, from_date)
    SELECT sheet_id, DATE '0001-01-01', person_id, grade, from_date FROM person_grade;

-- Each dated setting value recorded: it replaces the one recorded from the same from-date.
CREATE TABLE setting_history (
    id          BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    on_date     DATE         NOT NULL,
    setting_key VARCHAR(20)  NOT NULL,
    from_date   DATE         NOT NULL,
    setting     VARCHAR(20)
);
CREATE INDEX setting_history_sheet ON setting_history (sheet_id, id);
INSERT INTO setting_history (sheet_id, on_date, setting_key, from_date, setting)
    SELECT sheet_id, DATE '0001-01-01', setting_key, from_date, setting FROM setting_value;

A steward can now transfer a person to another sheet. The main "transfer person" test and scenario 1 pass in `bin/e2e`. Scenarios 2 and 3 still fail. They never call transfer, and they failed in the same place before I changed anything (details below).

**What the transfer does**
- **On screen:** each person's row has a new Transfer column with a sheet-id entry (`person-transfer-to`) and a button (`person-transfer`). A refusal shows the row's `person-error`, and taking any other action on the row clears it.
- **Refusals:** the transfer is refused for anyone but a steward, a retired person, this sheet's own id, and when the person's name, an alias or their contact is already on the other sheet. A refusal writes nothing. I also added two refusals the request didn't mention: a sheet id that has never been loaded, and an archived sheet.
- **Copied to the other sheet:**
  - The person gets a new id there. Their grades (with from-dates), terms, contact and aliases go with them, and their statement count starts at 0.
  - Claims keep their status, dates, notes, tags, settled figures and logs, in the same list order.
  - Claims that had a number get the other sheet's next numbers, in the order they were opened. Opening order is the sheet's today when each was opened, then the order they were added.
  - Figures a statement bound are dropped, and references are not carried.
- **Removed from this sheet:** the person, their claims, patron links in both directions, pool memberships, watches, holds, statements and closed-period figures. "Plans" don't exist anywhere in the app, so there was nothing to drop.
- **Audit:** this sheet writes `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … to=<sheet id>` followed by its rollup lines, and the other sheet writes `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … from=<sheet id>` followed by its own.

A few choices go beyond what the request spelled out:
- Claim comments go with the claims.
- If a transferred claim corrects, or was split from, another transferred claim, that link follows the new number.
- Locks and settle-batch numbers are cleared, since they belong to the old sheet.

**Why scenarios 2 and 3 fail:** both fail on `consolidated-people-count` while the sheet is shown as of a past date. The specs expect the consolidated figures to stay at today's values (3 people, and later 2 people with due 2.00 and overdue 2.25). At the same time they expect the header to follow the as-of date and show 0 people. The app today makes the consolidated figures follow the as-of date too, so they show 0. That is the consolidated feature's own behaviour, not part of this change, so I didn't change it. If you want those two scenarios to pass, the consolidated figures would need to always read today's data. Say if you want me to make that change.

The backend is in `TransferPerson.java` (new, plus `transfer.POST.yml`), with new methods `transferIn`/`remove` in `PersonRepository.java` and `transferAll` in `ClaimRepository.java`. The screen part is `features/transfer/transfer.slot.tsx`.
